headline: The foundation behind the main AI agent standards has loosened its rules so that younger projects and outside developers can join.
score_reason: Facts are an interview with one AAIF executive about changes made earlier (keynote in September); lowered 1 from 6 as older news and one-sided.
importance_line: It changes how open agent protocols such as MCP are governed and who may help shape them, affecting developers and companies building on them, though the account comes only from the foundation's own chief technology officer.
summary: Diginomica reports, in an interview with Manik Surtani, co-founder and chief technology officer of the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF), that the Linux Foundation body behind the agent protocols MCP and A2A has changed its rules. Projects now enter through a new "sandbox" stage with a six-month check-in and a 12-month review before a possible move to a growth stage, and working groups, once limited to member organisations, are open to everyone; the foundation has more than 270 members and says it will publish yearly counts of projects accepted, promoted and archived. These changes were announced at a September conference, so this is a later interview, not a new decision.
freshness: FOLLOW-UP of Sep 2026 (keynote day not stated)
notes: Lowered 1 as the rule changes date from September; the day is not stated in the article. MCP is the Model Context Protocol and A2A is Agent2Agent, both open standards for connecting AI agents.
